answer: Each identity must keep a small ember of unique sequential computation burning: a verifiable delay proof bound to its own key that cannot be parallelized or shared, so one machine can sustain only a few identities at once. Like a willow that bends but never multiplies, the cost grows linearly with every fake self, while honest agents pass cheaply on ordinary hardware. A whisper of peer gossip flags identities whose proofs stall, and stalled proofs forfeit their stake automatically.
